title: Trigger an eviction & explore memory limits
summary: Understand how Redis evaluates maxmemory limits, sample-based eviction algorithms (allkeys-lru, volatile-ttl), and memory fragmentation.

steps.title: Inspect memory allocation metrics
steps.explanation: Query INFO memory to view used_memory, maxmemory limits, and the currently active maxmemory-policy. Redis samples 5 keys per cycle to approximate LRU/LFU without global locks.

steps.title: Populate cache candidate keys
steps.explanation: Insert multiple candidate cache keys using MSET with the play: prefix. Each key allocates an internal dictEntry and sds value in the allocator.
steps.hint: Run: MSET play:cache:k1 "val1" play:cache:k2 "val2" play:cache:k3 "val3" play:cache:k4 "val4"

steps.title: Simulate memory pressure & check eviction policy
steps.explanation: Inspect the maxmemory-policy setting using CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy. Under policies like allkeys-lru or volatile-ttl, Redis evicts the oldest untouched candidates.
